title: Redwood Private VPC security architecture deep dive with Pioneer Credit
summary: Deep dive on Private / VPC deployment architecture focused on network isolation and security controls. Discussed SOC 2/ISO evidence, RBAC/SSO mapping, audit log forwarding, KMS/HSM options, and network ingress/egress patterns (NAT, private endpoints, firewall allowlists). Agreed next steps include sharing certs, network diagrams, and a POC kickoff window.
next_steps: Jordan to send SOC 2 + ISO27001 certs and security whitepaper
Elena to share proposed VPC peering/egress IP list for firewall allowlist
Customer to share internal network diagram and expected CIDR ranges
Schedule follow-up on-site network review & POC kickoff for 2026-03-03

Elena Ruiz - Provide VPC peering diagram and egress IP ranges for allowlisting - 2026-02-25
Priya Menon - Share Pioneer Credit internal VPC CIDRs and current firewall policy - 2026-02-23

transcript:
Date: 2026-02-20 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE); Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE) — Mark Hsu (CISO, Pioneer Credit); Priya Menon (Head of Cloud Ops); Liam O'Connor (Director, Infrastructure)

Summary: Quick intro, then 40m technical deep dive on Private/VPC architecture (network isolation, ingress/egress, firewalling, peering), followed by discussion on compliance artifacts (SOC 2/ISO), RBAC/SSO for admin access, audit log flows to Splunk, and KMS/HSM integration options. Some minor transcription errors present.

00:00 - Jordan Park: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, we'll keep this focused on the private VPC architecture and the firewall/egress questions Priya sent over.
00:22 - Mark Hsu: Yeah thanks Jordan, from my side I'm mainly interested in what isolation boundaries look like and how we can ensure no egress of PII to public internet.
00:35 - Elena Ruiz: Great, we'll start with an overview. Redwood Private runs a control plane and a data plane — in the VPC model customers can either use Redwood-managed private endpoints or deploy the runtime inside their VPC via our private agent. For Pioneer Credit we recommended the private agent model to keep all inference traffic inside your network.
01:15 - Liam O'Connor: Quick clarifying question — when you say "private agent" is that a container that runs on our EKS, or a VM appliance?
01:28 - Samir Patel: Good question — it's a containerized runtime (we provide kube manifests) but we also offer an OVA for air-gapped on-prem installs. The container path uses a small control channel to the Redwood control plane over a TLS mTLS connection if you opt into control-plane management; you can also run fully offline with local control if needed.
02:05 - Priya Menon: On the control channel: does that require outbound internet access from our subnets? We have strict egress restrictions and use a proxy with allowlist only.
02:18 - Elena Ruiz: You can configure either outbound through a customer-managed NAT/proxy with fixed egress IPs (we provide the list for allowlisting) or use VPC endpoints / private link to the Redwood control plane in our partner region. For fully air-gapped we exchange artifacts via an approved sftp and manual cert rotation.
03:00 - Mark Hsu: And audit logs — do you forward logs to our Splunk? We need immutable logs with retention controls for audits.
03:12 - Samir Patel: Yes, all runtime logs and audit events can be pushed to a customer SIEM via TLS, or written to an S3 bucket in your account with server-side encryption and Object Lock if you need WORM. We also emit detailed RBAC audit trails for admin actions.
03:50 - Jordan Park: To be clear on encryption: Redwood supports BYOK via KMS. You can either use Redwood-managed KMS keys or bring your own CMK stored in your KMS/HSM. For on-prem we support HSM connection patterns — we have a doc that covers PKCS#11 integration.
04:28 - Priya Menon: Does key rotation happen automatically or is it manual? Our policy requires quarterly rotation with audit.
04:37 - Samir Patel: We support both. Rotation can be managed by your KMS policies; Redwood will honor key aliases and will log the change events. For HSM-backed keys we surface rotation events to the audit log and you can require manual approval via your KMS.
05:10 - Liam O'Connor: Network diagram — how many subnets and IPs does the runtime require? We need to update firewall rules.
05:22 - Elena Ruiz: Typically the runtime needs one private subnet for inference nodes, one for control plane egress (if using managed control), and a transit subnet for shared services. We'll share a recommended CIDR layout. For firewalling you only need to allow egress to our control-plane IPs and allow inbound on the internal load balancer ports if you expose an internal API.
06:05 - Mark Hsu: If traffic is routed through NAT — do we get a static egress IP per region? Our firewall vendor requires fixed IPs for allowlist.
06:15 - Jordan Park: Yes, if you use our managed NAT gateway integration we provide a set of static egress IPs. If you run the agent in your VPC the egress IPs are whatever your NAT uses; Redwood can provide the hostname and IP ranges used by our control plane.
06:50 - Priya Menon: What about preventing accidental internet egress from the model payloads? e.g., model downloads or telemetry.
07:00 - Samir Patel: Model artifacts can be staged in your S3 or a local artifact registry in your VPC — the runtime pulls from there. Telemetry is configurable; you can opt out or route telemetry to your SIEM. We redact PII by default at the API layer but customers with strict requirements can enable full data-plane isolation and disable outbound telemetry.
08:20 - Liam O'Connor: Firewalling — do you require any inbound from our public zones? We prefer no public inbound at all.
08:31 - Elena Ruiz: No public inbound required. All nodes are private. If you need external integrations (e.g., external identity or SaaS connectors) we recommend using private link/VPC endpoints or a connector running in a DMZ that you control.
09:05 - Mark Hsu: On SSO and RBAC — how granular is the role model? We want separation of duties: ops vs security vs developers.
09:18 - Samir Patel: RBAC maps to fine-grained roles: admin, infra, developer, auditor. We support SAML SSO with SCIM for user provisioning so you can map groups from your IdP to Redwood roles. We also emit role-change audit events to your log sink.
10:00 - Priya Menon: Does it integrate with Okta and Azure AD?
10:05 - Jordan Park: Yes, Okta and Azure AD are tested. We support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, SCIM for group sync, and role mappings. We'll send the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoint details.
10:40 - Liam O'Connor: About network egress rules for external model fetching: if we host models in our S3, can the runtime avoid any external connectivity?
10:50 - Elena Ruiz: Yes, host models in your S3 and give the runtime an IAM role to access them. The runtime will not reach out to public registries unless configured. For offline installs you'll pre-stage the model tarballs.
11:30 - Mark Hsu: Compliance artifacts — can you share SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certs and also a pen test summary?
11:42 - Jordan Park: Absolutely — I'll drop the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts. We keep a redacted pen test summary; for full reports we can arrange an NDA if needed.
12:05 - Priya Menon: On audit log retention — can we push logs to our S3 with lifecycle rules? We need 7 years for certain records.
12:15 - Samir Patel: Yes, push to your S3 and set lifecycle/Glacier transition. We support log partitioning and can sign logs. Also support Object Lock for compliance retention.
12:50 - Liam O'Connor: For firewalling we want a fixed list of outbound IPs. Is that going to be stable or does it change often?
13:02 - Elena Ruiz: It's relatively stable; we roll small updates (rarely) and provide a changelog. For the managed control-plane endpoints we provide regional IP blocks; for private links it's an endpoint you control so nothing changes.
13:40 - Mark Hsu: What about DDoS protection — if there's a flood directed at the control-plane endpoint, does it impact our data-plane?
13:52 - Samir Patel: Control-plane DDoS is isolated; data-plane runs in your VPC so it's not in the same tenancy. For hosted managed control-plane we use CDN + rate-limiting and regional isolation. For on-prem/offline there's no external exposure.
14:35 - Jordan Park: Quick pause — any show-stoppers so far?
14:40 - Mark Hsu: Not yet. Just need the artifacts and the egress IPs to update firewall policy.
15:00 - Elena Ruiz: On encryption keys, a little more detail: you can bring your own CMK (AWS KMS) or manage HSM-backed keys on-prem. When BYOK is used we only store key references and use KMS APIs for envelope encryption; Redwood never sees plaintext keys.
15:35 - Priya Menon: For BYOK, do you support key rotation without downtime? We can't have inference jobs fail during rotation windows.
15:45 - Samir Patel: Rotation is seamless for new objects; existing in-flight sessions will remain using the existing encrypted material until they expire. We have handshake patterns to rewrap data with the new key. We'll surface a migration plan in the KMS doc.
16:30 - Liam O'Connor: Can we require HSM-backed signing for model artifacts? We need proof of provenance for models in production.
16:40 - Elena Ruiz: Yes, we support artifact signing via PKCS#11 HSMs and can validate signatures during model load. We'll include the signing flow in the docs.
17:15 - Mark Hsu: On network segmentation for different environments (dev/staging/prod), do you recommend separate VPCs or subnets?
17:28 - Jordan Park: We recommend separate VPCs per environment for strict boundary guarantees; subnets alone are ok but VPC separation is cleaner for policy and routing.
18:05 - Priya Menon: Any specifics about mutual TLS between our services and runtime?
18:12 - Samir Patel: We support mTLS for all control-plane channels using customer-provided certs or Redwood-managed certs; the runtime verifies certs at startup and during reconnects.
18:45 - Liam O'Connor: About firewall allowlist — is it IP based or FQDN? Our vendor only supports IP ranges for egress rules.
18:55 - Elena Ruiz: We'll provide stable IP ranges. FQDN is supported too but IP ranges are what we use for enterprise allowlists.
19:30 - Mark Hsu: For SIEM integration — what's the event schema? We need field names to map ingestion pipelines.
19:38 - Samir Patel: We have a JSON event schema and a mapping doc for Splunk/Datadog/Elastic; examples include event_type, user, role, action, resource_id, request_id, timestamp, and hashes for PII redaction. We'll share the schema.
20:05 - Jordan Park: Quick note — if Pioneer wants full private deployment (no control-plane egress) we can coordinate an on-prem bundle with manual upgrades. That's often used by banks.
20:20 - Priya Menon: That sounds like the likely path but need to evaluate operational burden.
20:35 - Liam O'Connor: POC scope — we want to validate network flows, audit logs to Splunk, KMS BYOK, and a sample inference workload. Estimated 2-week POC.
21:00 - Jordan Park: Sounds good. We'll propose a POC plan after this call.

(Transcript continues with intermittent clarifications — some stutters and mis-attributions)

30:05 - Jordan Park: I'll also include the security design doc and our control-plane IP ranges.
31:10 - Priya Menon: One more question on backups — does Redwood create backups of model caches? Where do they live?
31:20 - Elena Ruiz: Cache snapshots are optional. For private agent you control snapshot destinations (your S3). We can disable automatic offsite backups.
32:00 - Mark Hsu: On legal / procurement — we'll need data processing addendum with specific residency clauses.
32:10 - Jordan Park: Our legal team can draft a DPA with the residency and data handling clauses; I can introduce you to our legal contact.
33:05 - Liam O'Connor: If we do an air-gapped install, how do we handle security updates?
33:12 - Samir Patel: We provide signed update bundles and a checklist for offline patching. We also support a customer-managed patch pipeline.
34:00 - Priya Menon: Regarding admin console access — can that be restricted to a specific jump-host?
34:10 - Elena Ruiz: Yes, restrict via IP allowlist and SAML enforced conditions. You can require access through a bastion and enforce conditional access policies via your IdP.
35:00 - Mark Hsu: Are there any mandatory logs that Redwood keeps even in private mode? We need to know if anything can be disabled.
35:10 - Samir Patel: In private mode you control the logs; Redwood will not ship logs out. We do retain minimal operational metadata for billing if you use Redwood-managed billing; otherwise you can disable it.
36:00 - Jordan Park: Recap of immediate artifacts to send: SOC2/ISO certs, IP ranges, SAML metadata, SCIM endpoint, KMS/HSM integration doc, and the POC plan.
36:20 - Priya Menon: That covers it. Also please include a rough timeline and resources needed for the air-gapped install.
36:30 - Elena Ruiz: Will do.

Final 5 minutes: scheduling and next steps
48:00 - Jordan Park: We'll aim to send docs by Tuesday. Are there any calendar constraints for a POC kickoff week of 2026-03-02?
48:15 - Priya Menon: That week works for us; prefer Wed/Thu.
48:25 - Mark Hsu: OK Wed the 3rd or Thu the 4th is fine.
49:00 - Jordan Park: Great — Jordan to send calendar invite and artifacts. Elena will share the network diagram and egress list. Samir will put together KMS/HSM notes.
50:10 - Liam O'Connor: Thanks everyone, good session.
50:20 - Mark Hsu: Thanks — appreciate the detail.
50:35 - Jordan Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up.

Notes: occasional transcription errors ("privatee" or "k-m-s" instead of KMS) and some speaker labels are approximate.
